purpose: Test whether the existing non-billable Joel single-author idiolect features can safely predict cached Pangram-4 acceptance strongly enough to skip some future Pangram calls. This is a detector-call pre-screen calibration, not IER and not a human-authorship classifier.

profile.provenance: natural-owner-confirmed; each source owner-confirmed 2026-08-18 as zero AI help in state/IDIOLECT-CORPUS-SOURCE-INVENTORY-2026-08-18.json
profile.register_limit: Profile is current research/practical/polemical Joel prose and is not register-matched to every cached Romance or Spiritual Bypassing candidate. Treat that mismatch as a limitation, not a reason to tune the profile after seeing labels.

primary.definition: prediction_short == Human and fraction_ai == 0 and fraction_ai_assisted == 0

training_rule: Within each training partition, consider only monotone high-similarity rules from the allowed forms. A candidate rule must clear at least 3 training texts and produce zero training false-safes. Choose the rule with greatest training coverage, then lower complexity, then stricter thresholds as deterministic tie-breakers. Do not fit a global threshold on all data before held-out evaluation.

holdout_design.method: leave-one-article-family-out; exact text SHA deduplication before fitting; repeats never count as additional examples
holdout_design.reason: Most cache entries within one article are closely related edits. Random text-level splitting would leak near-duplicate article material and materially overstate predictive value.

primary_error: false-safe: rule clears a text to skip Pangram but cached Pangram primary target is not strict_full_human

substitution_acceptance.note: These are deliberately stringent because the proposed use suppresses a detector call. Failure means no substitution authorization; it does not mean the idiolect features are useless for anti-erasure review. With fewer than three independent article families the experiment may establish signal or feasibility but cannot authorize broad Pangram replacement.

privacy.allowed_output: hashes, measurement keys, article family, word counts, Pangram labels/fractions, idiolect similarities, fitted rule metadata, held-out predictions, aggregate error/coverage/confidence statistics
